facts.title: A Group of Owls Is Called a Parliament
facts.summary: A group of owls is called a parliament.

facts.title: An Owl's Face Works Like a Satellite Dish
facts.summary: The ring of feathers around an owl's eyes, called the facial disc, funnels sound toward its ears, and the owl can change its shape at will to focus sounds from different distances.

facts.title: Blakiston's Fish Owl Is the Largest Living Owl
facts.summary: Blakiston's fish owl is the largest living owl species.

facts.title: Burrowing Owls Use Dung as Bait to Catch Beetles
facts.summary: Burrowing owls scatter animal dung around the entrances of their burrows, and it works as bait.

facts.title: Great Grey Owls Can Hear Prey Moving Under 60 cm of Snow
facts.summary: The great grey owl can locate and catch prey moving beneath about 60 centimetres of snow, finding it by hearing alone.

facts.title: Great Horned Owls Are Among the Few Regular Predators of Skunks
facts.summary: The great horned owl is one of the few animals that regularly preys on skunks.

facts.title: Many Owls Have Lopsided Ears
facts.summary: In many owl species, the left and right ear openings sit at different places on the skull.

facts.title: Not All Owls Are Nocturnal
facts.summary: Most owls hunt at night, but not all of them: the northern hawk-owl, the burrowing owl and the short-eared owl are active during the day.

facts.title: Owls Can Turn Their Heads About 270 Degrees
facts.summary: Owls can swivel their heads roughly 270 degrees in either direction, letting them see behind them without moving the rest of the body.

facts.title: Owls Cough Up Pellets of Bones and Fur
facts.summary: Owls often swallow their prey whole and later regurgitate the parts they cannot digest, such as bones, scales and fur, as compact pellets.

facts.title: Owls Fly Almost Silently
facts.summary: Most owls can fly almost silently, letting them close in on prey that is listening for the slightest sound in the dark.

facts.title: Owls Have Forward-Facing Eyes Like Humans
facts.summary: Most birds of prey have eyes on the sides of the head, but owls' large eyes face forward, giving them stereoscopic vision and the depth perception they need to hunt in low light.

facts.title: Owls Have Twice as Many Neck Bones as Humans
facts.summary: Owls have 14 vertebrae in their necks, twice the seven found in humans.

facts.title: Owls Live Almost Everywhere on Earth
facts.summary: Owls are found in every region of the Earth except the polar ice caps and some remote islands.

facts.title: Snowy Owls Often Skip Breeding When Lemmings Are Scarce
facts.summary: In years when food is scarce, many snowy owls do not even attempt to breed.

facts.title: The Elf Owl Is the World's Smallest and Lightest Owl
facts.summary: The elf owl is the world's smallest and lightest owl.

facts.title: The US Approved Culling Invasive Barred Owls to Save Spotted Owls
facts.summary: In 2024, the US Fish and Wildlife Service adopted a strategy to remove invasive barred owls from parts of Washington, Oregon and California, to protect the threatened northern spotted owl and the California spotted owl.

facts.title: There Are More Than 200 Owl Species
facts.summary: Owls make up the order Strigiformes, which contains more than 200 living species; most counts put the total at around 220 to 225.
